phase1.explanation:
🦀 **Structs own their data unless they borrow it.**

**Ownership in structs:**

| Field Type | What happens |
|------------|--------------|
| `String` | Owned |
| `Vec<T>` | Owned |
| `&str` | Borrowed (needs lifetime) |
| `i32` | Copied |

**Rust-chan says:**
"Structs own their data. When a struct goes out of scope, all its data is dropped."

**Key patterns:**
| Pattern | Use |
|---------|-----|
| Owned struct | Full control, can be moved |
| Borrowed struct | Read-only access to existing data |
| Mutable borrowed struct | Read-write access to existing data |

 --> src/main.rs:13:30
  |
8 |     let player = Player {
  |         ------ move occurs because `player` has type `Player`, which does not implement the `Copy` trait
...
12 |     let name = player.name;  // Move
  |                ----------- value moved here
13 |     println!("Player name: {}", player.name);  // ERROR!
  |                              ^^^^^^^^^^^^^ value borrowed here after partial move

For more information about this error, try `rustc --explain E0382`.
phase2.explanation:
You moved `name` out of `player`. The rest of `player` is still valid, but `player.name` is no longer accessible.

**The fix:**
```rust
let name = player.name.clone();  // Clone instead of move
println!("Player name: {}", player.name);  // Valid
```

**Rust-chan says:**
"Moving a field out of a struct invalidates that field. The rest of the struct is still valid."
